reviews.author: Sherie G
reviews.text: We discovered a leak in our kitchen shortly after having new flooring put in.We live in a modular home and realized the belly bag was also filled with water. It was very stressful and we were so worried. We called Kamloops Stutters and talked to Aaron and we immediately came out to evaluate the situation. Then Mark came out and immediately got to work. He brought out 3 large fans and set them up. He also took all the wet insulation from the belly bag & placed fans under the unit. Once it was dried out they repaired the belly bag.They explained exactly which steps they would take and exactly what they would need to do each step of the way. Donna, Aaron & Mark kept in contact with us the whole time, relieving any stress we felt. We are very grateful for everything they did for us. Our house is now completely back to normal and we couldn't be happier. Thanks so much to Mark, Donna and Aaron for everything you did. We appreciate them so much!

reviews.author: Brenda Eisler
reviews.text:
We found ourselves in a very stressful situation where we needed help from a restoration company .Thankfully we contacted Stutters in kamloops bc .We spoke to Aaron who reasured us that help was on its way and that we would be looked after .Mark was here in clearwater by afternoon. Mark evaluated the situation and walked us
through the process. He had 5 large filter systems up and running to clean the soot from the air in are home .we had to leave the home .Mark was so informative and we felt releved knowing everything was in good hands!!!! Aaron was in constant contact with us He had 4 professional Cleansers. Belle,Amber,Tamara,and Stephanie. These women did such a great job cleaning our home ! Belle kept us informed of the progress .There where things that needed to leave the home to be cleaned and they looked after all of that for us.All of these women made us  feel that we where in good hands ,very thank full.Once we where back in our home mius many of are possession Aaron come out to clearwater and checked up on us and inform us that our thing will be coming back this week !! The whole team that we delt with were very professional and caring Thank you for being there for us and we will be recommending Stutter highly!!!

reviews.author: Annette Glover
reviews.text: After seeing some of these reviews I wish I had done a review when we got our kitchen cabinets.  It has been 25 years, but, the cabinets are still in great condition.  Every person who has worked in our kitchen since cannot believe how each new appliance fits as it was detailed built as well as the cabinets.  We needed an adjustment a couple of years ago and the Excel staff were very responsive to our needs and timing.  In addition with our 4 bathrooms, Excel provided all the cabinetry with the same performance standards. Thank you!

reviews.author: Shelley Mathes
reviews.text: Now that are kitchen is installed I felt it important to provide a review and a reason why I gave two stars based on our experience.  The design process was rather difficult because we were dealing with a "green" designer.  I understand that we all start somewhere, however, it made for a longer process in finalizing the design but none the less it did come together.  When installation took place we were left with an unfinished kitchen for months!  Not all cupboards were in at the time of install nor was the hardware, a cupboard door was the incorrect size and one of the dishwasher aprons didn't even touch the ground on one side. Finishing doors  on the sides of cabinets were hung incorrectly.  The paint of a router edge was not painted so we saw raw wood.  The third time that the installers came (the second was to install the rest of the hardware and doors) they told us  that the pull out that houses the knife, utensil full size cupboard drawer (very heavy) was not installed correctly and the entire drawer could have pulled out and dropped on our toes!  Thank goodness we asked why it wasn't opening evenly.  There were numerous errors beyond what was detailed above and when they were contacted about correcting them they were less than pleasant to deal with.  The lady that you deal with for  your deposit and payment was completely rude and miserable to deal with right from the very first conversation and any conversation there after was just as rude and  miserable.  I was recommended by a friend who is a local developer for residential development, however, I have to say I will not be returning to do any future projects nor would I recommend them.

During the planning stages of my dream home i called or went to about 80 businesses to get information and hire many, excel was by far the worst of them all, not just the worst kitchen place.

reviews.text:
We recently had the pleasure of working with Imagine the Room to improve the cabinetry in our new 700 sq. ft. home. With such a small space, storage is a constant challenge—but Tamy and Scott brought smart solutions and beautiful craftsmanship that made a huge impact.

The project began with widening the standard fridge opening to fit our 33” French-door refrigerator. What seemed like a small job quickly turned into a game-changer. Not only did they make the adjustment seamlessly, but the new cabinetry above the fridge added valuable space for storing cookware. The design and finish were flawless—matching our existing cabinetry perfectly, right down to the color and hardware. You’d never know it wasn’t part of the original build.

Later, when we realized we needed even more pantry storage, they returned and created a custom spice pantry in the narrow space beside the fridge. This brilliant addition transformed previously wasted space into a highly functional, easy-access cabinet that blends beautifully with the rest of the kitchen.

Living in a compact home can be complicated, but thanks to Imagine the Room’s vision and expertise, our kitchen now feels both more spacious and far more organized. Their craftsmanship, professionalism, and attention to detail exceeded all our expectations. Tamy and Scott are so easy to work with—it truly felt like a team effort.

We’re already planning more projects with them. Next up: the bedroom closet… and maybe the utility room too!

Highly recommended for anyone looking to combine functionality with stunning design.

reviews.author: Kimberly Grey
reviews.text:
I was travelling up hwy 5A on Wednesday September 28, 2022 at approximately 815pm.   I was on the section of the Hwy that was being milled.

There was absolutely no signage or cones to direct traffic.  There was a very large rut in the road which has caused significant damage to my car.

It was created by their removal of the existing surface through asphalt milling in anticipation of applying an overlay of fresh asphalt. This milling exposed the underlying gravels in the roadway which were eroded by traffic passing through them creating a pothole. This pothole and insufficient signage led to the damage our vehicle suffered.  They were trying to save money by not completing the required base repairs immediately after exposing them.

Because it was so dark I was unable to stop and take photos of the huge rut in the road and when I returned the following day (my husband drove me) the rut had been filled

My car now undrivable.  It will be repaired at a cost to me and but  this has left me without a vehicle until at least October 7th, causing significant hardship to my family.

When I spoke to John O'dare, he expressed very little care or compassion and BA Dawson has made no attempt to follow up with me or to provide any compensation.

I am shocked at the lack of willingness to provide any kind of support as this was completely their fault.

I have had to file a claim with ICBC but of course there is a deductible and the inconvenience.  I did try and rent a car but there are none available.

I have been around the road construction industry for a number of years and the quality of care and services that BA Dawson has shown me is shameful.

reviews.author: Michael Chala
reviews.text: We recently built a new outdoor kitchen in our backyard. True Concrete was recommended to us by another contractor we used, and he had informed us that there was new ownership. We met with Chris so that we could decide what countertop we wanted, i.e. granite, concrete, etc. Our first impression of Chris was that he was very likeable and easy to work with. He also showed us around his shop so we could see samples of his work. We were very impressed by what we saw. We immediately made plans with him to get us a quote and estimated time from first measurements through to install. The cost was considerably cheaper than granite and the time estimate was much quicker than anticipated. We committed to his services. Once our project was ready for the countertop, Chris and his son came up and took their measurements. They spent extra time double-checking measurements and asking questions of us, to be thorough as possible. They then built the countertop and delivered it to us in less than the time that was promised (2-3 weeks). The final product was gorgeous and it fit perfect. The two of them even lifted our 200-lb BBQ in and out of the opening several times, again to confirm accuracy and fit, until they were satisfied. Overall, it was a great experience for us. We would highly recommend them, their quality of work, their excellent communication with us throughout the process, and their personable approach, to anyone! Thanks, Chris!!!

reviews.author: Patrick Martel
reviews.text:
Funk Electrical is a great local company that you should seriously consider if you have any residential work to be done. When initially choosing the company to help me get my service upgraded from 100A -> 200A, I had called three companies to get a quote or any information on how to proceed. Without naming the other companies, the service I got was simply incomparable to what Funk had provided. The other companies had basically told me "Yeah you gotta figure out if you have the proper size conduit or not and we can go from there, call BC Hydro to figure that out and then call us back". I remember that Mike had taken my phone call while busy working on another project and set up a date/time to come by and learn the work I wanted to do.

When he arrived, I was really taken aback at how thorough he was and how much information he got from me, and how much information he gave me, especially compared to the experience I had with the other two companies that came by. He spent over an hour at my place without even having my business yet, and to me that showed how much he and Funk cares about understanding the needs of the client and wanting a full picture before committing to a project.

With that being said, I do want to say that they're not perfect, and nor is it realistic to expect them to be. Large projects like this almost never go to plan, and it's great when they do, but what matters most to me is how a company handles the situation when things do not go to plan. I had a couple minor issues after the service upgrade (old AC line was hooked up instead of the new heat pump, and the dishwasher hadn't been hooked up to the new breaker), and when I called Funk to tell them about the issues, they were either fixed on that same day that I called or within 24 hours.

Funk is a company that cares about their clients and their needs, and I 100% recommend them to anyone looking for any sort of electrical work. Thank you Mike and Phill for your work and I will definitely be seeing you guys in the future.

reviews.author: Michael Savage
reviews.text:
Harrison Industrial Contracting - Matt Jordan
First clarification Matt Jordan has recently purchased Harrison Industrial Contracting and we recently purchased a three horse Bison Trailer from him and his wife.

First: Caveat emptor
Caveat emptor is Latin for "Let the buyer beware". Generally, caveat emptor is the contract law principle that controls the sale of real property after the date of closing, but may also apply to sales of other goods.

We are culpable and should have returned the trailer immediately instead of trying to reach a fair discount for the repairs that would be needed to be done to make the trailer road safe! Instead we accepted "Stupidly a $2,500.00 discount." The repairs have now exceeded $7,000.00 and counting...

Second: "Full Disclosure" Matt's favourite catch-all saying that he had made full disclosure in his dealings with us and sadly that did not happen.

Now the facts:
2008 Bison 3 Horse trailer with living quarters
From Matt Jordan, its been used by me and my family has grown and we need a bigger trailer.

Everything is in good mechanical and working order including the fridge, freezer, microwave, kitchen stove, hot water heater, air conditioner, heater, batteries, propane gas system and interior lights.

Roof did not leak or have any leaks ever, the brakes had recently been replaced and were 60% or better and all electrical worked properly.

Matt's wife was continually wiping the floor to keep the water leaks hidden from us.

The brake drums were worn, grooved and exceed their specifications for wear. They had to be replaced. The brakes were worn and way beyond the 60% Matt has said they had for life... All brakes, backing plates, drums and bearing needed to be replaced.

The electrical wiring for the brakes had been torn-out and Mickey Moused back and the brakes failed before we hit the Coquihalla Highway and all braking was on our truck. Dangerous and serioulsy negligent!

We hit a serious rain storm and the trailer was soaked when returned home.

Matt made the comment and alluded that he had made "full disclosure" nothing could be farther from the truth or as one would reasonably expect.

In my opinion, I would not do business with Matt or Harrison Industrial Contracting.

If you do, I would be very careful about doing business with Matt and his company. Everything would be tightly documented with strict QA/QC controls and proper checks and balances in place before signing off and moneys paid.

More to follow on my blog

reviews.author: J H P
reviews.text:
My vehicle was heavily damaged when a dozer door they were hauling on Highway 1  flung open, shattering the glass door - with the glass flying towards my vehicle like a sheet of ice while doing 100 km/h coming up to a corner.

Though it’s hard to see, that thick, tempered glass ended up causing over $10,000 worth of damage to my vehicle - destroying my radiator, cracking my windshield and headlight, and cutting/scratching paint across my vehicle (even through the paint protection film). I’m glad no one got injured.

Blake, Extreme’s safety lead, was handling the incident from their side. He admitted to both myself directly and to ICBC that they were liable, but told ICBC that it was an “Act of God” that the door flung open.

All I wanted was for Extreme Excavating owners (Doug & JD) to pay for my $300 deductible, since Blake admitted their equipment was liable for the damage to my vehicle. Instead, Blake would not return my emails or phone calls. It’s important to note that Blake told me in person he used to work for ICBC, so he knows them inside and out - and any loopholes.

Let’s be honest, dozer doors don’t just fly open. It was either a) improperly latched/locked, or b) they had a faulty latch.

Instead of me leaving a positive review for taking care of my $300 deductible, I am leaving a negative review on how they handled the situation they admitted they were liable for.

Doug/JD, not sure if Blake did not communicate this to you or not, but I am happy to remove this negative review and leave a positive one instead if you are willing to cover my deductible.

Sincerely,
Patrick

Their obsession with banging on every single one of my outside doors) including a relatively hidden one) every single week day from 8AM-5PM. What do they want? I don't know. I have my reasons for not answering, yet still they persist. They don't seem to know what pen and paper are so no note is ever left in my mailbox. It's just bang bang bang all day, every day. They make a beeline towards me whenever they see me outside, they gawk at me from across the street, they have long conversations outside my home...the list goes on. I really don't appreciate being terrorised inside my home.

I anticipated the noise and water disruptions (even though the water disruption wasn't mentioned by the city...nor was tearing up my land), but what I didn't expect was having my privacy invaded every single day. reviews.author: John Cassels
reviews.text:
Title: Exceptional Performance and Hassle-free Maintenance!

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I recently had the pleasure of installing painless underground sprinklers in my backyard, and I must say, I am thoroughly impressed with the system's exceptional performance and hassle-free maintenance. These sprinklers have truly transformed my lawn care routine, and I couldn't be happier with the results.

From the moment of installation, it was evident that the quality of the painless underground sprinklers was superb. The materials used are durable and built to last, ensuring a long lifespan for the system. The installation process itself was smooth and efficient, thanks to the expertise of the professional team who handled the job. They paid attention to every detail, ensuring that the sprinklers were strategically placed for optimal coverage.

One of the standout features of this system is its intelligent programming capabilities. The painless underground sprinklers allow me to customize watering schedules based on my specific lawn's needs, taking into account factors such as the type of soil, sun exposure, and plant varieties. This level of customization ensures that my lawn receives the perfect amount of water, promoting healthy growth while conserving water resources.

Another aspect that sets these sprinklers apart is their reliability. Once programmed, the system operates flawlessly, consistently delivering water where it's needed most. I no longer have to worry about manually watering my lawn or adjusting sprinklers to compensate for missed spots. The painless underground sprinklers provide comprehensive coverage, evenly distributing water across the entire lawn with precision.

Maintenance is a breeze with this system. The sprinklers are designed to be self-draining, preventing any potential damage during freezing temperatures. Additionally, the components are of high quality, reducing the likelihood of clogs or leaks. The system's user-friendly interface allows me to easily monitor and adjust settings as needed, ensuring optimal performance throughout the seasons.

In terms of customer service, the painless underground sprinklers team has been exceptional. They were responsive to my inquiries, providing detailed information about the product and addressing any concerns I had. Their professionalism and commitment to customer satisfaction are commendable.

Overall, I highly recommend painless underground sprinklers to anyone seeking a reliable, efficient, and low-maintenance irrigation system. The quality craftsmanship, intelligent programming, and exceptional customer service make them a worthwhile investment. Thanks to these sprinklers, my lawn has never looked better, and I can confidently say that my watering worries are a thing of the past!

reviews.author: Marlon Dosch
reviews.text:
This will NOT be a good review of Richard Lemieux and Kami Hardwoods. Quite honestly I don’t know where to start so I will start at the beginning of our interactions.

At our initial consultations Richard mentioned that the project would take a week. Which was to replace the laminate on our stairs to hardwood, and have that hardwood match the existing flooring on the main level of the house. If we were to go ahead with the project we were to book dates with his wife Kelly Lemieux.
After talking with Kelly, Richard was to start on June 26, 2023 Monday at 8am.
We had discussed that the following week we were planning on making a trip to Calgary and was assured that the project would be done by the time we needed to leave.

On June 26, 2023 no one showed up at our home. I waited until 2pm and decided to call the office and got the answering machine, I left a message asking what was going on ? I thought Maybe I had made a mistake about the date.
When I didn’t get a response from my phone message I decided to write an email to Kami hardwoods asking them what’s up?
Turns out that I had the day right, Richard and Kelly had a communication problem regarding a job Richard was currently on. He would be at our place at 8 am Tuesday June 27, 2023 to start.  Finally showed up until 11:30am and the work started.

Even though the project was to be completed by the Friday, NOT all of the installation of hardwood was complete by then. So we pushed our trip to Calgary back so that the rest of the installation could be done, in addition to the finishing work. We emphasized over the past week to Richard that we must be on our way to Calgary by Tuesday that week. So he had Monday to complete the job.

Monday July 3. Richard completed the installation of the hardwood. Then he showed us a sample of the stain colour for the finishing. My wife thought it might work but I definitely did not think it was a MATCH to the existing flooring.  Richard went ahead with it anyway and once complete I told him I was not happy with the MATCH.  He become obviously upset and proceeded to clean up his tools and left without wanting to discuss it. He left very quickly and was clearly upset. ( see sample of match below)

July 4th,2023 Richard called asking where we were? Told him as discussed many times previously we were on our way to Calgary, and had to leave today.

He had left a bunch of equipment in our garage due to his ‘rush to get out of here’ , he mentioned he needed the equipment to work on other jobs.  We gave him the garage code to retrieve equipment he left behind .

On July 18th we called and left a message asking when the project was to resume. I continued to leave numerous messages, texts, and emails to Richard and Kami Hardwoods for the next 5 months without response as to when project would commence again.

During that time I did receive two invoices for the work done, I communicated back to Kami Hardwoods that payment was not going to happen until the job was completed.

I write this review on Jan 9th , 2024 a full 6.5 months after the project was to be started.  Our floor and stairs still don’t match. Needless to say we are getting quotes to rectify our flooring situation. I think we have given Kami Hardwoods more than enough time to communicate with us again.

We worked predominantly with Tracy, who was effective at communicating with us, sharing all sorts of helpful insight about tile type, color decisions, grout, tile sealer etc. great customer service.

In addition to advising us on tile choices, Walter from Kamloops Tile Works did the installation of our kitchen floor tile. He did an excellent job, especially considering these were 24"x24" inch tiles, and this house was built in 1955 so not perfectly straight or level. Note we purchased the backsplash and fireplace tile from Kamloops Tile Works and got these tiles installed by a different contractor. The kitchen floor terrazzo tile was purchased from a specialty shop in Ontario but was installed by Kamloops Tile Works.

reviews.text:
We can’t say enough good things about Five Oak Contracting.    From our initial contact with Five Oak, their first attendance at our home to listen to our wants and needs to refurbish our 28 year old home, to the end of the project, we have been totally satisfied with the attention to detail and open and honest communication with us.   Mike and Brandi made some great suggestions and helped us with our choices along the way.  They have a great working relationship with suppliers in Kamloops and as a result we had no delays waiting for products.  Five Oak works closely with Living Kitchens and has such a great relationship with them that they pre-book their installation dates for the entire year.   The upside of this is that when they took on our reno project we already had an installation date booked.  Living Kitchens and Five Oak helped design and fine-tune our kitchen and bathroom cabinets.  They listened to the specifics of what we wanted to see, made some great suggestions and our kitchen is perfect.  installation went without a hitch.  Quartz counters were manufactured and installed by Quattro and fit all cabinets perfectly.   Five Oak also works with Bridgeport Floors and with Brandi’s assistance we found the perfect floors for our home.   Bath and kitchen sinks and hardware were provided by another supplier Five Oak works with, The Ensuite and, again, with Brandi and Mike’s guidance everything turned out perfectly.    Brandi’s eye for design helped with our Benjamin Moore paint choices to bring everything together beautifully. Five Oak has an electrician and plumber they work exclusively with so there were no delays to the project waiting for sub-trades.   Our reno was a major one and we can say that Five Oak came in on time and on budget.  Their app they use was perfect for communication and allowed real time updates on daily progress and budget.  They guided us in making the choices we needed to make in time to have everything come together in a timely fashion.    We highly  recommend them for your renovation and would be happy to answer any specific questions you may have.   If you are thinking of a reno book them soon as they fill up fast.  We are thankful every day for our brand new, beautiful home.

Mike Boehm and Robin Russo

Madok Developments has been an outstanding builder to work with and a trusted partner on many residential projects over the years. Madok brings a strong knowledge of feasibility and budgeting, with an understanding of client expectations, which results in well executed homes that truly reflect the original design intent. They are detail oriented, organized on and off site, and great at working through challenges in a practical way.

I confidently recommend Madok Developments to anyone looking for a reliable, high quality residential builder.

reviews.text:
We couldn’t be happier with our experience working with Madok to build our custom home. From the very beginning, Murray and the team made the process seamless and stress-free. When we first reached out, all we knew was the location of where we wanted to build. Murray guided us through every step, starting with helping us purchase our lot, and then taking the reins to coordinate every detail, from initial vendor meetings to hiring and managing all the trades.

The attention to detail and commitment to quality from the Madok team was second to none. Murray was always available—just a call or text away—and kept us updated throughout the build. They ensured everything was completed to the highest standard and met our expectations at every turn.

We’ve been living in our home since March, and even months later, the exceptional support from Madok continues. Friends and family warned us about the challenges of building a home, but thanks to Murray, Kevin and Kara, our experience was nothing short of amazing. We can honestly say we didn’t have a single bad moment throughout the entire process—just positive, professional, and personalized service.

The quality of our home speaks for itself, and it’s clear that Madok Developments takes immense pride in their work. A heartfelt thank you to Murray and the team for turning our vision into a reality. Choosing to work with Madok was one of the best decision we’ve made as a family, and we highly recommend them to anyone looking to build their dream home.

reviews.author: Graeme Ward
reviews.text:
Of all the contractors I've hired ArmourGrade was by far the worst. Every time I walk outside I seem to find another problem. We had them replace gutters and soffit, here are just some of problems:

- Gutter leaks (they've attempted to fix one leak 3 times, after their third attempt I just fixed it myself).

- They don't know how to merge two pieces of j-channel together. Every joint around our entire house and garage is just two pieces overlapped, it looks absolutely horrible.

- Putting up soffit in a straight line over a 25 ft span? Not these guys. I cringe every time I look down the length of my garage.

- There are holes and gaps all over the place where animals can get into our roof.

- Water is getting down behind the aluminum facia they installed. During the last storm it was actually shooting a 4 ft stream of water out of the corner of the facia straight onto our deck. I've been told that shingle overhang was out of the scope of work. Here's my favourite bullet point from ArmourGrade's brochure when they sold me on the job: Inspect and ensure sufficient shingle overhang and drip edge.

- They installed a single piece of drip edge without asking me. The workers on site told me that they did it because they didn't think the shingles overhung the gutters enough. Right, like they are supposed to do (see above). A few days later they tacked on $168 to my final bill for it. A 10ft piece of drip edge costs less than $14. All they did was shove it under the shingles and walk away. In later discussion, I was told they actually installed 28 ft of drip edge. Their final invoice included drip edge installation, unit count 1, $168. I found the first 10ft of that 28ft long piece of drip edge, still not sure where the other 18ft went.

- Update, they came back weeks ago to fix more leaks, and put more drip edge up under the roof edge. They used MY drip edge, that I paid for. They actually said about the product I bought for a 15thof what they charged me "oh, this is better than what we use". Hilariously, they also said the drip edge that had previously been installed was not done properly. They were two of the same guys who had done the initial work. Said they'd come back to fix facia that overlaps the wrong way... it still overlaps the wrong way.

- When putting in a vent for a bathroom fan in the soffit they completely shredded the ducting on roofing nails. I didn't bother calling them about this one, I had to pull my fan out of the ceiling and rerun all the venting myself with the soffit already installed.

- I asked them to install black gutters and for all the drain tile caps at the bottom of the downspouts they installed white caps spray painted black on site. I asked them to get me black caps and they said this is what they always do and that they couldn't get black caps. I told them the paint would just come off and sure enough in a few months I had speckled white and black caps. I contacted their manager who actually told me that I should use better paint... what? This is a gutter company that can't get black drain caps, claims spray paint on plastic is an industry standard and when called out for it tells the customer to paint them again but with better paint than they used.

Anyone who has given ArmourGrade 5 stars needs to go outside and actually look at their workmanship.

I asked for a partial refund including compensation for the time I had to spend fixing their mistakes at the same rate I paid for additional labour on the job (either $80 or $100/hr depending on which employee you ask), and was offered $50/hr. When I said this was pretty insulting I was told that $50/hr is what they would pay a sub contractor, and aligns with industry standards. Should we do the math?

Hypothetically, let's say ArmourGrade sends someone to do 4 hrs of work on my house at $80/hr, and then I have to spend 2 hrs fixing their work and get reimbursed based on their ‘industry standard’:

-	The labourer makes $200
-	ArmourGrade makes $20 ($120 profit - $100 back to me)
-	I pay $220 and waste two hours of my time ($320 - $100)

Huh?

I recently had the pleasure of working with KTA Mechanical Inc., and I cannot speak highly enough of their exceptional service and professionalism. As a homeowner in Kamloops, BC, maintaining a comfortable and efficient home environment is paramount, and KTA Mechanical exceeded all my expectations.
During the peak of summer, my air conditioning system unexpectedly failed, leaving my family in discomfort during a particularly intense heatwave. In urgent need of a reliable HVAC contractor, I reached out to KTA Mechanical based on their stellar reputation in the community. Their prompt response was impressive; despite the high demand for HVAC services during that period, they scheduled a same-day appointment to assess the situation.
Upon arrival, the technician conducted a thorough inspection of my air conditioning unit. He was not only highly knowledgeable but also took the time to explain the issues in layman's terms, ensuring I understood the necessary repairs and associated costs. This transparency was refreshing and instilled a sense of trust.
The repair was executed efficiently, with meticulous attention to detail. The technician utilized state-of-the-art equipment, reflecting KTA Mechanical's commitment to employing the latest technology in their services. Within a short period, my air conditioning system was restored to optimal functionality, providing much-needed relief from the sweltering heat.
What truly sets KTA Mechanical apart is their dedication to customer satisfaction. They offer 24/7 emergency services, demonstrating their commitment to being there for their clients when it matters most. Their team is composed of certified professionals who are not only skilled but also courteous and respectful, ensuring a positive experience from start to finish.
In addition to their exceptional repair services, KTA Mechanical provides comprehensive maintenance plans to prevent future issues. I opted for their maintenance program, which includes regular inspections and servicing of my HVAC system. This proactive approach has given me peace of mind, knowing that my home's heating and cooling needs are in capable hands.
KTA Mechanical's reputation in Kamloops is well-deserved. Their unwavering commitment to quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction distinguishes them as a leader in the HVAC industry. I wholeheartedly recommend KTA Mechanical Inc. to anyone seeking top-tier HVAC services in the Kamloops area. Their expertise and dedication have earned my trust, and I will undoubtedly turn to them for all my future heating and cooling needs.

Jason nijjer

reviews.text:
3 stars because the tech was polite and easy to deal with. As for the rest of the service I was somewhat disappointed.

- I noticed that the suction on the vents was very weak telling me that nothing was getting sucked up. After the service was complete I could see on the techs 4 inch suction hose that there was a 3 inch hole in the hose near the vacuum causing a drop in line vacuum. Both the tech and I looked at it in disappointment as that was clearly an issue.

- I was told (and I have the call on my phone to prove this) over the phone that I would have the condenser coils cleaned on my a/c unit when they would come by included in the price. When asking the tech, the tech informed me that, that would be an additional 100 dollar charge.

- after cleaning i checked the furnace and noticed dust bunnies and thick dust on blower and surrounding components indicated it wasn't cleaned as advertised. The tech was nice enough to go back and redo this but I was disappointed that I had to check their work.

- I cant fault for this point as I did not ask over the phone but dont expect your dryer duct cleaning to be included in the price. Unfortunately that is another 100 dollar charge.

- also the disinfectant is.. you guessed it. Another 100 dollar charge.

- after leaving I checked the vents and Unfortunately they're still gross. So I guess after paying 620 with tax. I will be redoing the job myself.

Overall the points I appreciated:

- Tech was friendly
- Appreciated the tech went back to clean the furnace

Points that disappointed:

- hidden costs
- False advertisement by call staff
- vents didnt even come out clean
- Having to check quality of work (this bothers me because how many other times has this happened)

UPDATED REVIEW

The owner got ahold of me and is making it right and sending someone out to redo the job. He was very kind and appreciative.

I understand mistakes happen it just depends how theyre made right.

Update!!
I have cameras with time stamps that have your crew arriving at my house at 9am, leaving for over an hour for lunch, and packed up and rolling out at 230pm. I suggest you have a look at your 'trackers'. And how you could charge approx $1600 for labour and what, $300 for materials for 30ft of pex, a few fittings and a laundry box with taps is incredible, even of it was your claimed hours. But moreover I stand by my original remarks that transparency in billing options would have gone a long way!

I'll start off by saying that their workmanship and crew were great, but I'm not at all satisfied with their billing practices. Was told by the guy doing the quote, 2 guys for the day, quote was for just shy of $1900. Job was completed in 4.5hrs of them being on site, bill still came to quoted amount. I called asked for a breakdown of the quote to which I was told they don't have that information but I had agreed to the quote and that was that. She did however, tell me they COULD have billed me by time plus parts but it was too late. This was never mentioned as an option and she didn't seem to appreciate it when I suggested that this should all be made aware to their clients to add transparency and fairness. Apparently I'm the 1st to complain about this, and yet I see plenty of complaints about billing here. It's too bad, I was looking forward to having them in to service our new home.

reviews.author: Shane Carroll
reviews.text:
I've been using Sinclair for my business for over sixteen years. As a tradesman I find the knowledge base of this company to be outstanding. When I, as a professional need advice I can always turn to the men behind the counter to offer me insight and technical data. For warranty claims, Sinclair goes above and beyond always!

They carry items the other local wholesalers often fall short of. If you are a professional, they will extend to you ever courtesy, they cater to professionals exclusively, and will happily provide you with needed information, and even recommendations to get your projects done, safely, legally, and professionally!

I have to make an addendum to this review.

I've been a loyal Sinclair customer for many years. Of late, I seriously have to question where the people who manage this company are going. The loss of Tim and Gene in the Kamloops branch is demonstrative of an exceptional disconnect between the people in charge, and the people on the front lines. The amount of knowledge between Tim and Gene no longer being at this branch cannot be replaced. These people have been in this industry for ages, and are extremely well known and appreciated for their personalities, honesty and integrity. I know the loss of these people will have a negative impact locally for this branch. I'm very disappointed in the direction Sinclair is moving in.

reviews.author: Mike
reviews.text:
Older guy behind the counter was rude and arrogant. Wanted to buy a couple of grommets for my furnace and he asked if I was ticketed, to which I replied “you need a ticket to change a grommet”? He had no response other than to essentially ask me to leave.  I could understand his hesitation to sell me a gas valve or something like that but grommets??
It looks like Sinclair has developed a bit of a reputation in town and it doesn’t sound like a good one. I get what they are attempting to do “protecting” contractors in the area but I doubt they are accomplishing much other than costing themselves sales and encouraging bad reviews. Most people that want to do this kind of work themselves have the resourcefulness to figure out to try other local businesses or buy what you need from a business online. I always try to buy locally first and was able to find the parts I needed in Kamloops, but have purchased online in the past and usually at a lower price.
Their refusal to sell to the public seems somewhat discriminatory too, considering that a homeowner has the right to pull permits and do their own work provided they can show they are capable of doing the work. This came directly from an inspector.
All I wanted was a couple grommets. It’s not rocket science to change them, and there is no risk involved. No permits are required. I think the attitude of the guy behind the counter annoyed me even more than his refusal to sell me the part, completely unnecessary.

reviews.text:
First experience with this company.

We first inquired about Grubs, and the lady who came to look was nice, informative and friendly. Ultimately let us know that it wasn't, and there wasn't anything much to to be done. That's fair.

Payed for 4 visits in the spring. Gave us no indication of the schedule, but the 2nd visit only came in July which seems a little late?

So the lawn care guy. Very young fellow who I can only describe as being extremely disinterested in the job. No response when I said hello, and did it so quickly that he left before I could even get to the back to remove kids toys. Not impressive.

My grass at this point was suffering from a lot of yellowing spots (despite watering frequently with irrigation system) no doubt from from all this heat, but I would have liked to have talked to the fellow about some seed and good coverage of fertilizer or at the very least talk about how we could make it look better.

So we decided to cancel the services as I feel I can do the same job for much cheaper with the same results or better. To be fair, the office did offer a different tech to come back out right away along with a free service add-on so I am happy to say that they tried to help us, but I would have liked to have had some service and care for the price I payed towards my lawn from the start.

reviews.author: Art Babin
reviews.text: As anyone who has built a house knows, there are a lot of very important decisions to be made.  Design, colours, products, contractors, the list goes on and on.  One of the best decisions we made was to use Sirocco Landscapes to design and build our landscaping.  It included xeriscaping, retaining walls, paving stones, irrigation, a pergola, front and rear decking, fencing, lighting and a fire bowl feature.  Although our property isn't a huge one, the project presented a number of challenges because of the house design and natural grades.  Spencer was able to identify the potential issues and offer suggestions on how to deal with them before providing a quote.  In any  big project things don't go exactly as planned.  When this happened, Spencer and his team ensured we were kept up to date with any issues and changes that needed to be made.  Spencer's detailed design and quote meant we were ensured we weren't going to have any surprises at the end of the project.  In the end, we are very happy with how it all turned out.  We are often receiving compliments from friends, family and complete strangers on how nice the landscaping is.   We've had a couple small issues over a year after the installation which have been rectified very quickly and to our satisfaction.  Sirocco Landscapes has left us very confident that they will be there to take care of us in all our landscaping needs going forward.  I would highly recommend Spencer, Stephanie and their team to anyone needing their services.

reviews.text:
Recently had a really horrible experience with this shop. My truck was having engine issues, a of couple other shops had trouble figuring out what it was, so I took it to Brys. The other shops only touched electrical whereas Brys took the valve cover off. They diagnosed it as a camshaft (engine replacement recommended). I limped the truck home in far worse condition than I dropped it off in. The whole truck was shuddering, the check engine light was now flashing and I honestly didn't think it was making it home. I called them and they said that it would get progressively worse. I got home opened up the hood and noticed hose clamps just loose in the engine bay. I reattached them and tried calling brys repeatedly. They wouldn't pick up. But when my friend called immediately after they picked up for him. I don't think I was an unpleasant customer. I even brought these guys donuts the day they started working on my truck. I paid over a grand and I got the truck back running way worse. I took it to another mechanic who found that there was a broken valve spring. Something that Brys should have caught. The valve cover had not been tightened down, half of my spark plugs (all of bank 2) was switched to Bosch eventhough they only had 3 hours on them. The spark plugs were not gapped and the firing order was incorrect. I went back to ask for my money back as they had misdiagnosed my truck and caused further damage. I'm not sure what exactly I paid them for? They are now saying that Brys automotive doesn't exist anymore. That it's bankrupt and that the first mechanic to work on my truck at Brys now owns the shop. His son has now gone around saying that I "only want free work done to my truck". I paid every other shop without question because eventhough they did not fix the problem, they did install functioning parts and did not cause further damage to my truck. I even tipped the mechanic who actually fixed my truck. I also reached out to tkemlups bylaw to find out if they were lying about pulling a different business license.  According to an email thread with bylaw, Brys had not had a business license at any point since moving to the reserve. I also have proof of Bry's claiming to have a business license when they did not. This shop is incompetent and lacks accountability. I wouldn't let these guys work on a lawnmower, let alone touch another one of my vehicles (even if they offered to do it for free 😂).

Thankfully my truck is fixed (for a fraction of the price they charged me to damage my truck). Hopefully this prevents someone else from falling victim to this shop ❤️

reviews.author: Amber Glennie
reviews.text:
If I could give negative stars I would. In January 2021, our basement flooded due to a broken water main. We were recommended On-side restoration for the repairs, It is now August of 2023 and we are still dealing with this nightmare of a company. From the beginning there were missed appointment dates, months with zero contact or updates, and a multitude of lies and blame shifting. Devin was our project manager, and let me tell you the review below calling him "the worst" is no exaggeration. I think the fact he has been let go from the company is clear proof of his inability. After multiple attempts to communicate with Devin, we finally had to get in contact with his manager Andrew Scott. We arranged a meeting to sit down with both Devin and Andrew and go over some of the issues we were having.

During this meeting Andrew explained that there were some staffing issues and that  Devin was not getting the support from the company that he needed. We made a list of the things that needed to be addressed: The vanity that was damaged by OnSides technicians needed to be replaced, a wall had to be repainted, and the new floors were lifting behind the toilet .  We discussed at length with them the frustrations we were feeling with lack of communication and the time it was taking them to fix three rooms. We were ensured by Andrew that they would be taken care of, and moving forward we would have regular communication.

Fast forward a few months, I think about October, the vanity that was damaged by Onsides technicians was finally being replaced.They hired a third party to install the new vanity , and when transporting the vanity into the house, they did significant damage to a vehicle in the garage. Now to give some context about this vehicle, it had never been in the garage. The car arrived at the house in July after having the engine rebuilt and a whole bunch of other work done. From July to September the car was in the driveway, we had to bring the car into the garage because winter was right around the corner, when they finally arrived in October to fix the vanity that they broke, they scratched the side of the drivers fender and the drivers door.

We were told the damage would be assessed and there would be compensation for said damage. One day we received a letter in the mail asking for payment of the deductible. As far as we are concerned the claim is not finished as the damage to the car has not been assessed. We voiced this fact to both our insurance company and the restoration company, and are told to get a hold of the territory Manager (Jeff) I contact him, explain the story for what feels like the 100th time and am advised he will personally look at the damage to the car, the first week of August. It is now August 17, are you surprised we haven't heard from him ? So almost two years later we are left with VERY POOR QUALITY repairs and a damaged vehicle. On side refused to sign any sort of document claiming fault for the vehicle, after verbally agreeing they would. They are now claiming the car is in too poor condition to notice new damage, even though Devin came to our house and photographed said damage. Instead they have threatened to send the owed deductible to a collection agency, which will in turn damage our credit score.

Some other losses that we took include 12 months of rent that we lost on our basement suite ($9600), two days of wages lost waiting for a water tech and cleaning tech that stood us up ($336), our laundry machines were left disconnected for almost 5 months and we had to do dry cleaning for that entire time ($1200) and now our scratched car ($1500-2000). So in all we are at about a $12,000-$13,000 loss. Thanks On-side!

0 out of 10, would not and will never recommend to anyone, ever.

Here are some pictures of the car they claim in poor condition and the workmanship they claim as "quality"

Geoff was very reassuring and left us with the feeling that we had found the "right" service provider.  The abatement crew members were skilled, professional, and efficient.  The project started on time, communication was good, and the project finished on time.  The attention to detail was very good.  If you're looking for someone to do your asbestos abatement (or any of their other services), you will do well to seek a quote from WINMAR. reviews.author: Matthew Perera
reviews.text:
My town's Best Buy does not have a Geek Squad, so I travelled to Kamloops. I was looking for a new laptop that would suit my education needs: including video creation, programming, 3D design, and AI development.

Getting there by medical bus was simple. There is an entrance from outside that is wheelchair accessible, as is the entire store.

There were a few customers ahead of me, but the wait was only ten minutes. The GS employee had difficulty understanding what I was saying, at first, but was straightforward enough to help me decide to salvage my drives and recycle my old laptop.

Another associate helped me look into getting a new device. It took about twenty minutes, due to the complications of rural shipping addresses, and the inability of Best Buy to have my new computer shipped to my local branch... All they could do was try to send it directly to my home. Nevertheless, they gave me a significant discount on an already discounted, lightly-used open box product that suited my needs, as well as on the protection plan. That is greatly appreciated!

After that, the Geek Squad member returned to help me find the peripherals I needed to access my extracted drives.

I feel that the two employees who helped me tried to be courteous, but seemed skeptical at first, perhaps thinking that I might be a homeless person. I have Osteogenesis Imperfecta, am ambulatory, and in even mild winters I wear a snowsuit to keep warm enough, and dry if I fall while standing.

I recommend their employees be trained in interactions with PwDs (if not already), and engage customers by the latter's actions rather than their clothing.

Other than that, I think it was a good experience. I will look to them for my tech needs in the near future.

reviews.text: Extreme lack of communication. Ordered an Apple Pencil, when the order was placed at the store, was told January 2nd it will arrive. Got there Jan 2nd and they told me the order hasn’t been placed yet and will arrive sometime from January 5th-6th. Keeping in mind it was placed on December 30th and the pencil was coming from Vernon. Got a call 10:30 January 5th saying my pencil has arrived and is ready for pick up. Got there at 11:30 and they said it wasn’t there, and accused me of fabricating the phone call, even after showing them the call logs and calling the number in front of them bringing me to Best Buy Canada’s answering service. Not sure who the manager is there, but he shrugged off and said there isn’t anything he can do. So after 2 trips and 2 failed times to get my order they still can’t get anything right. Hours of my time driving and in store  wasted, fuel there and back and still nothing yet. Disappointed it has been this way, will never use Best Buy again.

I have used Look Out Landscaping for fall and spring yard cleanup and have always been happy with the work .

I am very grateful that I did not have to call and ask when they would send someone....they were on it before my a.m. coffee was finished brewing.

This made my day in more ways than one. My driveway and sidewalks are clear and ready for the contractor I have coming today!!

Great job. More than pleased.

reviews.author: Trevor Svedberg
reviews.text: This is the WORST company, highly recommend NOT using them. I had the worker here for under an hour with cameras proving this. The employee said he would charge 1 hour for being here and shook my hand. When I got my bill, they charged me for an hour and a half visit. When I called them about it, they were extremely rude and hung up on me! When I called back to speak to the owner the woman I spoke with was very hostile. When I mentioned the cameras though, her tune changed. She said she'd look into it, called me back shortly and changed her mind. I mentioned that I'm sure I'm not the first person this has happened to. Sure wish I would have looked at their Google reviews before booking them. This company is labour gouging and NOT honest. Call anywhere else for your landscaping needs.

reviews.author: Matt Klassen
reviews.text: LOOK OUT FOR LOOK OUT LANDSCAPING. This company is the worst landscape company in town. They were working on the house next to mine and trespassed onto my property and clear cut my entire tree and flower bed. They cut down a very old cedar bush 3.5m tall, took out multiple flowering bushes and another large cedar. They followed that up by acting like it wasn't a big deal and offered to replace my beautiful trees and flowers with some rock covering. Then the next day they did work on a fence that connected to mine and completely destroyed my side of the fence as well with no offer to fix any damage. These crews have 0 idea what they are doing or even whos property they are working on. After they had already made multiple mistakes the foreman had the audacity to say that I was lying about what happened. Bad crews. Terrible supervisors and even worse management! I imagine these guys are no strangers to being in court for all the mistakes they make. STAY AWAY!

reviews.author: Lorna Anolik
reviews.text:
The word professional doesn't mean the same thing to me as it does to this company. What landscaping company doesn't have a grass catching bag on their lawn mower. This one doesn't, and left furrows of cut grass on the lawn. The one older lady did an awesome job weeding and cutting back branches, albeit slower than it should have taken her. The list of less than professional work as follows:
- 2 people had to take the debris tarp to the dump.  Why?
- one girl I found did a lot of standing around watching the other two workers, and raked as slow as molasses
- why would you weed whack the same area that had just been done by a co-worker?
- who blows leaves off a gravel driveway when the leaves are still falling while they are doing this?

My issues are very valid as both my daughter and SIL are professional and certified landscapers who have their own company at the Coast, and who were disgusted at the slowness of raking and weeding, and appalled at the standing around of one particular worker. On top of that, this company charged twice as much as they would have realistically charged for the same service at the Coast where they can charge higher rates. Their professionalism is evident in every job they do! So no I would not recommend this company to anyone...they are not the professionals they claim to be, nor do they perform professionally, or perhaps this type of work is now the new standard for professionalism. Either way, we were not impressed!!!

reviews.text:
Sadly, I had a pretty bad experience here. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND that you get quotes in writing and in detail. I called to inquire about having my forklift cylinder rebuilt. I was asked about the size and type so I explained the cylinder was approx 48" long x 5" diameter and also explained that the cylinder had some minor nicks in it. The owner quoted me $500-$600 dollars assuming that the piston was straight and all it needed was chroming, polishing and seals.

To be clear, this cylinder didn't drift or leak any appreciable amount. As this seemed affordable, I decided to remove the cylinder and bring it in. A couple of days later I got a call that it would be $1100 plus tax. As can be understood, I was shocked as I included the seals that I already had for them to use so I expected it to be at worst less than $600 unless it needed other work or more parts.

I inquired as to why it was DOUBLE  the original quote. She explained the cylinder needed a little welding on the end and rechroming. I explained that this was extremely far from the quote and asked why, as with the exception of an hour of welding and machine time at $125/hr, this didn't add up. I never did get a straight answer or explanation other than it needed more work.

It was clear to me that despite it needing a small weld repair on the very end of the piston and rechroming, there just wasn't any legitimate reason for the massive discrepancy between the quote and the revised quote. As a result, I retrieved my cylinder in pieces, paid my $250 bill, for essentially nothing except disassembly. I really feel lied to and misled, like once they had your item, they could charge as they pleased and you basically were stuck. I regret not having gotten it in writing and not checking their reviews. Lesson learned, I have quite a few other pieces of equipment that I intend to have redone,  looks like the coastal shops are the ones getting my business from here on forward.
So much for supporting local 😕

reviews.author: David Cruz
reviews.text:
Very disappointed with this business, hired them to come in and tell me what needed to happen in order to fix a commercial aluminum/glass door combo that was rubbing on the frame.

The quoting representative came in and quoted the fixture of the door as a glass re-install, trueing of door frame and finally a replacement of door hinges quote.

He was queried if this would fix the door to which his reply was yes, I approved the quote and the work commenced.

That is where things started to fall apart, when the installers came in they said they trued the frame and installed the glass, but did not replace the hinges and they quoted "They don't make 4 inch square commercial hinges anymore" so they re-installed the door with the old hinges which were shot and tweeked it so that it would not touch the frame.

Proceeded to request payment on the account and basically stipulated that the door was not fixable.

Well that would have been useful information before they quoted to fix the door with no reservations.

I searched on the net and found the commercial hinges easy enough, when it was mentioned to them that there is hinges in that size and commercial application, they said if their suppliers don't carry them, they don't even bother with looking looking for them.

Now to get them to come out and complete the job, was a job in itself, they did not want to come out to replace the hinges until some persuasion had to be used in order to get them out again, as a matter of fact they wanted to charge another fee to come out and and complete the job for which they quoted, after they left the door was working only to start touching the frame again within a couple of days.

When brought to their attention they said never guaranteed that it would work. Yikes! I thought I was hiring professionals, not people who would change the parameters of the original contract and then would try to use hidden non existent fine print to cover their initial mistake when quoting.

I have paid the bill even though I probably look like a sucker.

I agreed to pay it upon completion which I have and that is what I gave my word on, they however did not complete the job properly and have requested I pay them again to come out and fix what they did not fix the first time.

I have been in business 30 plus years and this is not the way to do business!

It looks like now I am going to have to pay again, for someone else to fix what they did not. What a joke!

Buyer beware!

reviews.author: Renee Keddy
reviews.text:
We got our new kitchen installed almost 5 years ago. Blaire never came out to see the finished kitchen. Once the last nail was put in they were gone.
The trim on the top of the cabinets is not squared at the corners. Sylvia told us to keep the metal stack that goes from the hood vent to outside. The installer refused to build us a box around the metal stack. He just covered the hole by putting the cupboard to the top of the ceiling. He advised us to go and get a hood vent with an exhaust that blows outwards instead of upwards. Which we did. Now our townhouse has so much moisture in it by covering up that vent.
Now almost 5 years later our cupboard doors are all bubbling at the bottoms. We can’t have a pot of boiling water on the stove without water running down the cupboard doors.
We had been trying for weeks to try and get a hold of Blaire. Finally we got Sylvia to come over and take pictures to show to Blaire. Still no response from Blaire. We spent a month going back and forth to the store to say that he had not responded to us.
My husband finally got a hold of him by phoning the Vernon store. He told Blaire about the installer not making a box for the vent. He stated why we hadn’t told him about that earlier. Why didn’t he come out after the kitchen cupboards were installed to see how the job looked? Poor business etiquette. He then told him about the cupboard doors with water damage and chipping. He stated that we must have done that ourselves and that the warranty only covers the mechanical parts for the hinges on the cupboards and drawers. That’s bullshit. We didn’t spend over 15 thousand dollars on a kitchen only to have it replaced 5 years later.
Poor business. I would not recommend this company to anyone.

After losing our home to wildfire, the idea of rebuilding felt overwhelming—so many decisions to make, so much uncertainty. But then I contacted Jen. I gave her a rough idea of the vibe I was going for, and by our next meeting, she had already created detailed drawings, selected a gorgeous colour palette, and offered thoughtful options that fit perfectly within our budget. It was as if she understood my needs better than I did.

Jen designed our kitchen, master bathroom, laundry room, and pantry. The installation was on time and seamless. Even when we made a few mistakes on our end, Norelco patiently and promptly resolved them without hesitation.

I’ve never owned a kitchen so practical and beautiful. Jen is hands-on, professional, creative, responsive, and patient. She brings both technical know-how and a brilliant design sense that truly turns kitchen dreams into reality.

Thank you, Jen & Norelco for taking such impecable care of us and for helping to restore our lives after the devastation of the fire.

After struggling to even hear back from several cabinet companies we decided to give Spectrum a call since they had such good reviews. We learned why when we met Steve.

Steve's motto is something like, "I want to do a good job so that if you ever see me at Costco you want to come over, say hello, and shake my hand," and he 100% delivered for us. This was one of the best customer service experiences we've had with any business of any type.

Steve and his team from Spectrum have been in this industry for a long time and we really valued their design input and knowledge. They gave us a lot of options, prepared samples of possible materials, and were patient and relaxed throughout the design process. reviews.text:
We bought our house 18 months ago and as part of our renovations we added a roof over the back deck and had the vinyl decking and railings replaced (both were 25 years old) as well as the railing for the outside basement entrance. We hired Kelowna Deck & Rail after getting four quotes. Most of the estimates were very close and our builder recommended Sven of Kelowna Deck & Rail.

Lewis removed and installed the new vinyl and did an excellent job. He was very polite and very professional and was in two and half days. Sven, the owner, and one of his team installed the new railings and it took them about half a day.

Sven was very communicative and a pleasure to deal with. He and our builder coordinated directly, making this one last thing we had to manage.

We highly recommend Kelowna Deck and Rail.

We have no hesitation in recommending their service and workmanship.

The Nailed It guys truly live up to their name. The process of working with them from start to finish was just wonderful and we couldn’t be happier with our bathrooms.

The quotes were accurate and we were never hit with any hidden costs or surprises (any changes in price due to spec changes, at our request, were always okayed in advance). Ashton, Richard, and the rest of the team were responsive to messages and questions. They were all consistently kind to myself and others working on the property—even despite less than ideal working conditions—and kept the site clean and their working area contained and tidy.

Evan was our primary on-site worker and his high bar for quality shows. We had a particularly finicky fluted tile and it was cut to perfection, seams were considered in layout and lined up, and you can see the level of care that was taken in installation.

It feels like we’re entering a spa or hotel every time, a total luxury. We would work with Nailed It again in a heartbeat, thank you guys!

Each member of the Nailed It team was professional, friendly, and delivered excellent quality workmanship throughout our home. The vinyl flooring continues to be functional and looks fabulous.  It’s easy to clean.  We have absolutely no issues with the flooring or the installation.  Thanks Conrad!

reviews.author: Tanya Thompson
reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Review for Talon Environmental Services

We cannot say enough good things about Talon Environmental Services.

From the moment they became involved, it was clear we were dealing with true professionals who care deeply about doing the job properly. Their team was thorough, methodical, and incredibly knowledgeable. They took the time to explain what they were seeing, why it mattered, and how they would address it — never rushed, never dismissive.

What stood out most was their attention to detail and integrity. They didn’t just remove what was obvious; they followed the evidence, documented everything clearly, and made thoughtful, justified decisions based on site conditions. Their documentation was exceptionally clear and professional, which gave us real confidence in the work being done.

Communication was excellent throughout. We always knew what was happening, what the next steps were, and why. They were respectful of our home, careful with containment, and left the site clean and well managed.

Most importantly, Talon gave us peace of mind during a very stressful situation. Knowing that the remediation was done correctly and independently verified made all the difference.

If you are dealing with mould, water damage, or environmental concerns and want a team that is competent, ethical, and genuinely invested in getting it right, we would recommend Talon Environmental Services without hesitation.

RAVE!!! Huge shout out to Talon Environmental Services Inc. I was in a real predicament, and without hesitation—no questions asked—they swooped in and found exactly what I needed to solve the issue.

I reached out to 4 abatement services in Kelowna and chose Talon to remove drywall containing asbestos from our character home.  Jaime and the entire team were professional, organized, and great to deal with.  Communication was good and Tyler, the crew manager also payed attention to small details of the job and spent time with me going over what was to stay in place and what was to be removed. Jaime arranged monitoring with Epoch so that was part of the logistics I didn't have to concern myself with.  In the end, 260 bags of abatement material were removed from the house.
If you are unfortunately faced with an abatement project I wouldn't hesitate in recommending Talon Services.
Thank you Jaime and your team.

reviews.text: I can't say enough good things about this place.  Around Christmas my 35 year old furnace failed. I decided to pull the offending assembly ("draft inducer" - didn't even know what it was).  Well, took it down to Central Elec, and they jumped on the task of trying to find a new assy (motor+fan housing) right away.  Took them a few days and a lot of effort, but they managed to find the only mfr in N.America still making the part.  I prepaid it and they got it on order, and by the time it arrived these guys had somehow found a way to significantly cut the cost down.  Instead of keeping that info to themselves, they credited my card for the savings they'd found!  This is next-level customer service.  Re-installed the part (an exact match) and it looks like we're good for another 35 years.  Thanks guys!

Quick summary in this paragraph for those not interested long stories. I have had great experiences with Gescan Abbotsford. I moved out to the Okanagan and mainly dealt with Gescan Kelowna. I was working on a project where things kept changing on me and I ended up with too many relays. I returned the extras and forgot about it until the next tax year when I noticed I hadn't been credited. Life is busy and it wasn't my top priority so it took time to finally contact them about not crediting my account. Now there's no record, no proof of anything. 6 relays at $58.01 per relay plus tax. So they've got my money for the relays and the relays as well.

More details for those interested. When I returned the relays everyone up front was busy so a guy came out from the offices grabbed them from me. We chatted for a couple minutes. I said something like "that's it, we're good?" He says to me "I got you buddy". I don't know about you but when somebody tells me I've got your materials, we're good, I figure its all good.

So this was all back in mid 2018 and it was a year by the time I noticed I wasn't credited. Now I've got a baby due and getting my money from Gescan is the furthest thing from my mind. I forget for a while longer and  then it's early 2020. I contact the Manager of the branch and he's somewhat helpful at first but then doesn't respond to my email. I now try to go up the chain but get directed back to the branch manager. He says he never got my reply. It's possible, ok fine. We chat back and forth. I provide my original invoice as well as my invoice I billed out to my customer showing how many relays were billed for. After the back and forth it finally comes down to "show me the proof of return" a piece of paper signed by the person who took the items from me.... I never got anything except verbal confirmation. Feels like he knows that I can't prove anything and this is how you nicely say screw off. Why did it take multiple emails to get to this point?

Alright, I know when I'm beaten. But I won't spend another cent at a Gescan ever again and maybe I can influence others to do the same. I closed my account with Gescan and now I deal with wholesalers that actually credit my account when I return items.

reviews.text:
On December 5th, Andrew Newby solved a big problem for us. His actions saved us from a rather expensive alternative.

Some background: Our Amantii electric fireplace stopped working last week after seven years of reliable performance. We contacted the store that sold that appliance to us to be informed that repair service is not available, only sales and parts! We were advised to obtain the services of an electrician and subsequently called Holmes Electric.

Within minutes of arriving, Andrew was able to restart our fireplace and it has worked perfectly since then. He informed us that the most likely cause of the problem was another space heater which had kicked in at the time we turned on the fireplace heater. That other baseboard heater, located in our garage, was never utilized but we didn’t realize the thermostat activating it was not turned off. reviews.author: Owen McGinn
reviews.text:
I want to take the time to review my experience with this business. I bought a battery on Dec. 4th 2025 and brought it home to put into my UTV. First thing I notice was the battery had a top or side mount feature, with two different size bolts. As my application needed to have the top mount, I would need to use the shorter bolts. When I took the flat nuts out of the package to insert into the battery terminal, they were shorter ( not as thick) and the short screws just barely meant the top of the nut heads and with two main leads and two accessory leads one to each terminal, the screws were no where close to reaching the threads of the nut. There was no room to slip in anything to raise the nut up. I put the longer bolts through in order to reach the nuts, and wonder! Why are they not using thicker nuts like the ones that were in my last battery? They could have a nut that is twice the thickness taking away the inability to reach threads, having to try and jack the nut up with cardboard, silicone etc very poor design! When I put the longer bolts through and tighten it up the bolts bottomed out and pushed the terminal up and the design of having both a side and top post, has a weak point and a terrible molding design which only leaves 1/8” corners on one side of the battery, guess what happened, yup! The terminal gave way! I am 62 yrs old built many classic vehicles have had 20 different types of motorcycle, 10 different types of snowmobile, dozens of cars, trucks and never have I seen a battery, with the amount of pressure added, break like this.
I knew I could fix it with proper solder, solder paste, and application and setup, and did in the end.
My problem is the stores attitude to focus on a problem that I don’t feel was the problem, maybe the reason for the problem coming to the surface but not the problem. I tried to explain that yes I did try and use the the longer bolts on the top mount but I don’t feel it was tighten to a point where the post should have given way and cracked across both (weak)corners. I feel the problem was a molding problem ( poor casting) and poor fasteners inadequate size nuts, as the nuts should and could be thicker allowing the nuts to sit higher on the top post mount allowing leads for main and accessories to be mounted while still reaching the threads on the nut, without having to try and jack the nut up to get at the threads. When the person at the front counter met was starting to piss me off so badly as they only seemed to have one thing on their mind, NOT OUR PROBLEM! I could have bought this battery at CT, Costco, and many other big box stores and returned it with no issue but I choose to shop local. These are the types of business that wreck it for local type businesses. It’s fixed now, with no help from this local business, I wouldn’t buy another thing from them. I am putting pictures in to show the difference in the size of their nuts and other battery nuts, check the corner post.
All I can say is this business needs to readjust their business sense and attitude, towards service and customer input.

His attention to detail and knowledge of home-construction, building code, best practice and safety was evident throughout.

All too often, we hear horror stories of hidden gotchas, poor workmanship and unethical practices / billing when dealing with fly-by-night contractors. Even more concern arises if one is left at the mercy of a fast-talking tradesman who tends to rush their work for the sake of speed and profitability. Andrew is an excellent electrician and stood by his word for price, timings, thoroughness and the delivery of the services I asked of him. Andrew met and exceeded my expectations. Working with Andrew, there were no surprises, no hidden costs and every aspect of his service was exactly as advertised. I prefer the best surprise is no surprise approach that Andrew clearly takes.

The manner in which Andrew conducts himself and serves his clients should be the standard by which all professional tradesmen are judged. Andrew is a consummate professional and you really can’t do better when selecting your electrician in the Kelowna area. reviews.text:
April 27, 2021
We have been using our Hybrid Elevator for almost 2 months & have been meaning to write a review. As you may have noticed we have given a 5 star rating. I would love to mention all of the names of everyone who was involved but there are others who are constructing these elevators behind the scenes who would not get their dues. Everyone that we had contact with was professional, helpful & treated us with respect & importance. The elevator was installed within 2 weeks with no inconvenience to us & it was put inside our home. DCR Contracting had the hoistway, which includes all of the outside walls, doors, dry walling & painting, done within 5 days & completed it at the end with the finishing touches. We barely knew he was here other than that he was there to answer many questions with a professional, knowledgeable & kind manner. He protected everything from the dust, cleaned up every day & the finished job was spectacular. Ours was a difficult installation as we had half floors with a total of 3 stops. It looks beautiful & works quietly & effortlessly. We keep asking ourselves why we waited so long. I could go on & on about Hybrid’s & DCR’s workmanship, design of the elevator, how little impact it has on our home other than the ease it is to get from floor to floor & the beauty the elevator has added to our lives (both physically & mentally). Everyone that comes over
gives overwhelming praise to the construction & efficiency of the elevator & hoistway. We are getting older & mobility is getting a bit harder but now with our new elevator we can stay in our home & our neighbourhood. Sandy M
